truong-xuan-cung-hqp-ngu: A brand-new painting of a natural, lived-in, richly furnished room, painted exactly like image 1 (the bedroom): same hand, same brushwork, same soft painterly finish, same natural warm colours, saturation and contrast, same depth with furniture, curtains and objects arranged through the whole room from the foreground to the back. Wide panoramic, eye-level view, summer morning. ROOM: Trường Xuân cung chính điện bedroom, the private bedchamber of the Imperial Noble Consort (Hoàng quý phi), the highest consort below the Empress, in ancient China, a real room in daily use, seen straight on with the back wall straight across the picture and the right side wall running towards the viewer in clear perspective, meeting at a square corner; dark zitan pillars and beams with gold lacquer; the main subject is a grand walk-in canopy bed (a babu bed: a bed built like a small carved room with its own front porch and a carved openwork front gate) standing against the back wall, centred, square to it and seen straight on, the large clear main subject, its carved front gate open, bright orange silk curtains lined with golden yellow tied back inside, bright orange silk brocade bedding with golden yellow borders, embroidered with white magnolias and a pair of small phoenixes, pearl strings on the gate; to the left of the bed, flat against the back wall, a tall folding screen with kingfisher-blue feather inlay and magnolias; to the right of the bed a carved openwork partition with a tall vase-shaped doorway giving a glimpse of a dressing room; tall carved lattice windows in the right side wall onto a sunny courtyard garden with a magnolia tree; along the walls a gold-lacquer dressing table with a tall bronze mirror and a jewellery cabinet open with pearls and jade, a zitan curio shelf of jade, coral and cloisonné treasures, ornate hanging palace lanterns with orange tassels, a clothes stand with an orange silk robe, cloisonné vases of magnolia branches, a gold incense burner, slippers on the bed porch step. Trường Xuân cung signature style, the same in every room of this palace: white magnolias (ngọc lan) are its flower, painted on the screens, embroidered on the silks and in the vases; borders of the endless swastika fret and round longevity medallions carved in the beams and furniture; dark zitan sandalwood with gold lacquer and mother-of-pearl inlay; square-backed zitan furniture (never round-backed); a tall vase-shaped doorway (never a round moon gate) in a carved openwork partition; screens with kingfisher-blue feather inlay. HOÀNG QUÝ PHI level, the Vice-Empress (phó hậu, owner Lượt 572): nearly as splendid as the Empress, only one small step below her: rich gilt carving everywhere on the furniture, gold lacquer, mother-of-pearl, pearls, jade, coral, cloisonné and kingfisher-blue inlay, many treasures; the main seats and the bed look imperial and throne-like, with tall carved gilded backs and gilded frames, close to the Empress's own.  COLOURS (owner Lượt 584, rank colours: Hoàng quý phi = ORANGE + yellow): warm bright orange is the main colour of the silks, with golden yellow as its partner: bright orange silk bedding and seat brocades with golden yellow borders and embroidery, orange silk curtains lined with golden yellow, orange and gold tassels; yellow clearly LESS than in an Empress's room (only borders, linings, embroidery and gilt); no red silks, no red bedding; the wood stays dark zitan with gold lacquer. Phoenixes allowed: a pair of phoenixes carved and gilded or embroidered among magnolias on the bed, the screen and the cushions, and a pair of small gilded phoenix figures. ROOM SHAPE (owner Lượt 491): the room reads rectilinear with square corners, straight walls and straight beams, never a curved hall, never furniture in an arc or a curve; every piece of furniture stands in clear straight lines along the walls, square to the walls, orderly, never scattered and never at a slant. Keep the same room, the same arrangement and the same distance as image 3 (this same room as drawn before): the same walls, windows, furniture places and size; change only the colours as written here. LAYOUT NUMBERS (owner Lượt 477, 491, 520): seen as in image 3, the furniture fills about five sixths of the room, the main piece large with its base reaching down to about seven eighths of the picture height; the open floor in front is only a strip of about one tenth of the picture height at the centre, and nothing stands on that strip, because people will stand there. The right corner is furnished, never empty or bare: a table group stands there inside the outer fifth of the width, set back from the bottom edge, between one half and seven eighths of the picture height, so a person standing in front of it covers it naturally. FLOOR: warm polished wooden floorboards visible between the furniture, no large rug or carpet covering the floor (at most a small mat under the bed porch step); the walk-in canopy bed sits in the central half of the width. LIGHT: soft warm morning daylight from the right, like the light on the girl in image 2, so a person standing in the room looks lit by it. Do not leave the room empty like a stage; it should feel natural and furnished, people will simply be placed in it later.
